D009-D001_h001.question:
It’s hard to explain because it feels like this has just always been how my brain works. Even back in primary school, teachers told my mum I “never stopped talking,” that I’d blurt answers out, jump from one thing to another, and stare out the window instead of finishing work. I’ve always talked fast; my thoughts seem to race ahead of my mouth. I remember lying in bed as a kid, wide awake at 2 or 3 a.m., mind just running, not really feeling tired, then dragging myself through school the next day.

That restlessness has never really let up. As an officer, I pace during briefings, tap my feet, fidget with pens; sitting still in long meetings is torture. I’m constantly shifting tasks, starting reports and then getting distracted by something else. People say I interrupt and talk over them, or jump from topic to topic.

Over the last year, though, I’ve felt mostly down—like the joy’s been sucked out. Even when I hit milestones in my career, I just feel numb, like it doesn’t matter. Thinking feels like wading through mud; concentrating on planning or paperwork exhausts me. I get these recurring thoughts like, “What’s the point?” and sometimes, “It’d be easier if I just didn’t wake up,” though I haven’t made any plans.
D009-D001_h001.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Bipolar II Disorder
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    D. Anorexia Nervosa

D009-D001_h002.options:
